title: What things cost
summary: Every sum the Bible names, in days of a labourer’s wage. The New Testament gives its own yardstick: a denarius for a day in the vineyard (Matt 20:2). The Old Testament gives a year’s wage of ten shekels (Judg 17:10), and Hammurabi’s laws a thirtieth of a shekel a day. On these figures, silver wages rose about tenfold by the Persian period, so a shekel did not buy the same work in every book. Each sum is reckoned in the money of its own time. The figures in the text are the text’s; the days are an estimate, and say what they rest on.

yardstick.hours: A working day is twelve hours: “Are there not twelve hours of daylight?” (John 11:9), and the vineyard’s eleventh-hour workers worked one hour (Matt 20:6, 12).
yardstick.year: ≈300 working days make a year’s wages: a six-day week less the Sabbaths and festivals. The BSB counts a talent of 6,000 denarii as “about twenty years’ wages” on the same reckoning (Matt 18:24 note).

gold.basis: Gold is reckoned at thirteen times its weight in silver, as Herodotus does for the Persian empire’s tribute (Histories 3.95). No ratio is stated for Israel; it is the nearest ancient figure, and is applied to every gold sum given by weight.

eras.label: Before the exile
eras.basis: A day’s wage was about a thirtieth of a shekel of silver. Hammurabi’s laws pay a hired labourer six grains (she) of silver a day for the first five months of the year and five after, and 180 grains make a shekel (§273). Micah pays his Levite ten shekels a year with clothes and food (Judg 17:10), which is ten shekels for ≈300 days’ work. The figure is applied from Genesis to the fall of Jerusalem, though wages surely varied over those centuries.

units.name: shekel
units.basis: A weight of silver, about 11.4 g (the BSB’s figure).

units.name: gerah
units.basis: Twenty gerahs to the shekel (Exod 30:13).

units.name: beka
units.basis: “A beka per person, that is, half a shekel” (Exod 38:26).

units.name: pim
units.basis: Two-thirds of a shekel: a stone weight of about 7 g found in excavations (BSB note on 1 Sam 13:21).

units.name: mina
units.basis: Fifty shekels, a sixtieth of the 3,000-shekel talent. Ezekiel’s mina is sixty (Ezek 45:12), and Kings and Chronicles together imply a hundred (1 Kgs 10:17; 2 Chr 9:16).

units.name: talent
units.basis: 3,000 shekels: Exodus counts 603,550 half-shekels as 100 talents and 1,775 shekels (Exod 38:25-26).

units.name: daric
units.basis: A Persian gold coin of 8.4 g (the BSB’s figure, Ezra 2:69), at thirteen times its weight in silver: about 9.6 shekels.

eras.label: After the exile
eras.basis: ≈ A drachma a day. The Athenian accounts for building the Erechtheion pay labourers, architect and sawyers a drachma a day (408/7 BC), and Tobit offers his son’s guide “a drachma a day” (Tob 5:14). No wage is recorded for Persian Judah itself. On these figures silver bought far less work than in Hammurabi’s day: a shekel now paid for days, not a month.

units.name: drachma
units.basis: The yardstick: a day’s pay.

units.name: daric
units.basis: Twenty drachmas: Cyrus the younger paid “three thousand darics” for a promised “ten talents” (Xenophon, Anabasis 1.7.18), and a talent is 6,000 drachmas.

units.name: talent
units.basis: The Babylonian talent, in which the empire’s silver was weighed: “seventy-eight Euboic minae” (Herodotus 3.89), or 7,800 drachmas.

units.name: Euboic talent
units.basis: The talent Herodotus reckons the empire’s tribute in: sixty Euboic minae of a hundred drachmas.

units.name: mina
units.basis: A sixtieth of that talent.

units.name: shekel
units.basis: Sixty to the mina, as Ezekiel reckons it (Ezek 45:12): about 2 drachmas.

units.name: assarion

units.name: quadrans
units.basis: A sixty-fourth of a denarius (BSB note on Matt 5:26).

units.name: lepton
units.basis: Half a quadrans: two lepta “amount to” one (Mark 12:42), a 128th of a denarius.

goods.name: sheep
goods.basis: Half a shekel, the Hittite laws’ price for a sheep (§178), at a thirtieth of a shekel a day: rams, ewes and lambs alike.

goods.name: goat
goods.basis: Priced as a sheep: the Hittite price list gives none for a goat.

goods.name: bull
goods.basis: Five shekels, the Hittite price of a bull (“ten half-shekels”), for the bulls, oxen and cattle the text offers or eats. The list’s dearer plough-ox was a draught animal, which none of these were.

goods.name: cow
goods.basis: Three and a half shekels, the Hittite price of a grown cow (“seven half-shekels”).

goods.name: year’s work
goods.basis: Paid in labour: ≈300 working days a year.
